# northstar robotics

ok so basically Northstar Robotics (founded 2022, HQ in Bengaluru) builds warehouse automation —
mostly autonomous pallet movers and a routing engine that tells the robots where to go without
bumping into each other lol. we started as a 3-person team out of a garage and now we're at 34
people, most of em engineering.

Rohan Mehta is the founder and CEO. He was previously at a logistics startup that got acquired (he
doesnt like to talk about it much, something went sideways there). Rohan's the one who pushed hard
for the "boring reliability over flashy demos" philosophy — he says a robot that works 99.9% of the
time and fails BORING (just stops, doesn't crash into a shelf) beats a robot that's 99.99% flashy and
1x catastrophic per year.

engineering is led by Priya Nair, she joined in year 2 after Rohan basically begged her to leave her
job at a much bigger robotics co. Priya owns the whole stack: the routing engine, the fleet
coordinator, and (reluctantly, she'll tell you) the firmware team since nobody else wanted it.

Sales/customer stuff — thats Sara Kim's dept, she came from an enterprise SaaS background, no
robotics experience going in but she's picked it up fast. Sara's closed most of our first 6 logo
deals personally.

## what we actually sell

Two things really:
1. the hardware (pallet movers, charging docks, safety beacons)
2. the routing engine + fleet software, which is honestly where the moat is — anyone can build a
   robot, not everyone can route 40 of them through a warehouse without gridlock

We charge a per-robot monthly fee plus a flat platform fee for the routing/fleet software. See the
pricing doc for actual numbers (they change every quarter lol, sales hates me for this).

## customers (early ones)

Finch Logistics was our first real customer — mid-size 3PL, they run 3 warehouses in the south, took
a chance on us when we were basically pre-revenue. Sara's been managing that relationship personally
since day one and there's a renewal coming up, see the deals doc.

We've also got two smaller pilots running but those are NDA'd so not gonna write details here.

## culture / random notes

- we do NOT do 9-9-6, Rohan is pretty firm about this after burning out at his last co
- stand-ups are async-first, live standup only happens tuesdays (see meeting notes)
- "boring reliability" is basically our whole engineering religion at this point, priya says it in
  every design review

## funding

Raised a seed round in 2022 (undisclosed-ish, but its "low 7 figures" per Rohan when he's had a
drink), and we're currently fundraising a Series A — targeting close sometime this year, no firm
date. Growth story is basically: prove the routing engine works at Finch's scale, then go sell to
bigger 3PLs.

anyway thats northstar in a nutshell. ping priya or rohan if this doc is out of date, i (whoever's
maintaining the wiki this month) probably havent touched it in a while.
